facts.fact_text: According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he arrived at Kaluzhskaya Square in Moscow to take part in the 'March of Millions'.

According to the applicant, at around 6.50 p.m. on 6 May 2012 he found himself near Malyy Kamennyy Bridge in a crowd surrounded by police officers who were beating the protestors with truncheons and arresting them.
According to the applicant, a police officer attacked him using a truncheon on 6 May 2012.
According to the applicant, he tried to protect himself from the blows by extending his arms forward and distancing himself from the police.
According to the applicant, four police officers eventually grabbed him and escorted him to a police car, which took him to a police station.
When police officer Mr G. approached the young man, the latter hit Mr G. on the left wrist.
The video recording depicted the young man striking police officer Mr K.'s head with the umbrella.
On 22 October 2014 the applicant was arrested.
On 26 February 2015 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow ordered the applicant's house arrest until 6 April 2015.

On 27 February 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence and destruction of property).
On 27 February 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
On 22 December 2015 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant guilty as charged.
The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment.

On 27 February 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence and destruction of property).
On 27 February 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
On 3 April 2015 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
The relevant provisions of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation can be found in Frumkin v. Russia, no. 74568/12, § 78, 5 January 2016.
The case concerns the applicant's criminal conviction for acts of mass disorder and violence against the police during the suppression of a demonstration at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow on 6 May 2012.
Police officer Mr G. testified on 19 May 2012 that the participants of the acts of mass disorder had shouted slogans.
Police officer Mr G. stated on 19 May 2012 that neither he nor his colleagues had sustained any injuries as a result of the actions of the participants of the acts of mass disorder.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that unidentified participants of acts of mass disorder threw chunks of tarmac, stones, sticks and other objects at the police, which hit them.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant used violence against Police Officers K. and G. which did not endanger their life or health.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant, acting with the intention of using violence, tried to prevent police officers from arresting aggressive participants of the demonstration.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant used violence against Police Officers K. and G. which did not endanger their life or health.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant, acting with the intention of using violence, tried to prevent police officers from arresting aggressive participants of the demonstration.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the applicant hit Police Officer G. at least once in the left hand, causing both Police Officers K. and G. pain.
The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment.

The applicant's sentence of two years and six months' imprisonment was calculated on the basis of a two-year prison term under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, partly concurrent with a term of one year and six months under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
